expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No, 'not empty' is insufficient. That test would not have caught this incident — you had rows, they just contained wrong values.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: Your `COALESCE(x, 0)` converted a screaming failure (NULL = "join found nothing") into silent plausibility. The system's natural error signal got muted.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Recommends only internal checks: tolerance bands, schema contracts, freshness/completeness checks. No external reconciliation (e.g., compare dashboard revenue against upstream system, Stripe, or actual business records).

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: Row count / sum assertions at transform time and Schema contract tests in CI that fail upstream deploy are both before-publication controls.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: Schema contract tests — Register expected column names/types. Fail CI when upstream changes break contracts before they reach prod.

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Add tolerance-band assertions and expected row count within range. Freshness + completeness checks not just 'rows exist'.

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: No mention of the three-week silent failure, monitoring gap, or why alerting failed to catch this. Treats only the technical root cause (COALESCE masking), not the detection infrastructure failure.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Your `COALESCE(x, 0)` converted a screaming failure into silent plausibility. The system's natural error signal got muted. (Implies people act on wrong numbers but catch loud failures.)
